item.title: Indiana bill would ease residency rules for Marion County public defenders
item.description: Marion County’s public defender office is struggling to fill long-vacant positions as a bill moving through the Indiana Statehouse seeks to ease residency requirements.

item.title: Metrobloks says its data center is not Big Tech, but Martindale-Brightwood residents still tell them to 'go home'
item.description: A Metropolitan Development Commission examiner is scheduled to decide whether to recommend the rezoning request for approval on Feb. 12.

item.title: Indiana bill aligns state with Trump administration’s immigration enforcement goals
item.description: Indiana lawmakers overhauled an immigration bill Monday to further align with the Trump Administration’s immigration enforcement policies.

item.title: Lawmakers want to ensure doctors get patient consent before performing some invasive procedures
item.description: Lawmakers want to require informed patient consent for some medical procedures. A bill moving through the legislature would bring Indiana in line with federal recommendations.

item.title: Lee Hamilton, towering figure in national politics with deep ties to IU, dies at 94
item.description: Lee Hamilton, a 17-term congressman serving southern Indiana, whose foreign policy expertise, reverence for democracy, and bipartisan ideals made him a towering and highly respected figure in national politics, died Wednesday. He was 94.

item.title: Franklin food pantry uses 'food rescue' to weather hard times
item.description: Food pantries in Indiana and across the country look to local grocers, college students, churches, K-12 schools, restaurants and bakeries for donations of food, or grow their own on rooftop gardens, or spend hours writing grant requests to stay afloat.

item.title: Indiana governor launches group to root out fraud, abuse in federal social safety net programs
item.description: Indiana leaders will give “extra” scrutiny to Medicaid and other federally funded, state-administered social services programs as part of a new entity focused on fraud, waste and abuse.

item.title: Insurance companies are fining hospitals for out-of-network care. A new bill aims to stop it
item.description: Insurance companies are fining hospitals for out-of-network care, arguing that federal changes are costing them more money. A new bill aims to stop those fines and protect consumers

item.title: Lawmakers weigh scope of doxxing bill after redistricting threats
item.description: The legislation would criminalize the tactic of releasing personally identifiable information with the intent to cause someone fear or harm — or encourage another person to do so.

item.title: 'Hailey’s Law' and Bears Stadium key issues as session hits final stretch
item.description: Speaker Todd Huston (R-Fishers) discussed key legislative priorities as lawmakers head into the back half of the session. “Hailey’s Law” and a new Bears Stadium were top of the list.
